claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Maizels and Gause, 2023; Smallwood et al., 2017) and represents established knowledge.

claims.claim: Helminths have developed immunoregulatory pathways characterized by an expansion of Treg, elevated levels of IL-10 and TGFβ, immunoregulatory monocytes and B-cell class switch to IgG4.
claims.source: To be able to establish chronic infections and promote their survival within the host, helminths have developed an array of immunoregulatory pathways, characterized by an expansion of Treg, elevated levels of IL-10 and TGFβ, immunoregulatory monocytes and B-cell class switch to IgG4, associated with immune tolerance (Maizels et al., 2018; Gazzinelli-Guimaraes and Nutman, 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Maizels et al., 2018; Gazzinelli-Guimaraes and Nutman, 2018).

claims.claim: A balance between the Th2 and the Treg responses is likely to be essential to allow the survival of both host and parasite.
claims.source: A balance between the Th2 and the Treg responses is likely to be essential to allow the survival of both host and parasite since an excess of either would damage the host due to pathological fibrosis or severe parasite burden (Harris and Loke, 2017; Everts et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Harris and Loke, 2017; Everts et al., 2010) and represents an inference about host-parasite dynamics.

claims.claim: Infection with Echinococcus multilocularis attenuates colitis in mice through the expansion of colonic Tregs, partially mediated by a shift in microbiome composition resulting in elevated levels of SCFAs.
claims.source: For example, it was recently demonstrated that infection with an extra-intestinal helminth, Echinococcus multilocularis, attenuates colitis in mice through the expansion of colonic Tregs. This effect was partially mediated by a shift in microbiome composition, resulting in elevated levels of SCFAs (Wang et al., 2023a).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2023a, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: Helminth excretory/secretory products (ESP) comprise all the molecules that are actively released or produced as waste throughout their life cycle, including proteins, small peptides, enzymes, lipids, and glycans, and they are specific in species and stage.
claims.source: These ESP comprise all the molecules that are actively released or produced as waste throughout their life cycle, including proteins, small peptides, enzymes, lipids, and glycans, and they are specific in species and stage (Maizels et al., 2018; van der Zande et al., 2019; Sobotková et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Maizels et al., 2018; van der Zande et al., 2019; Sobotková et al., 2019).

claims.claim: Hp-TGM exhibits potent immunoregulatory properties, including the expansion of Tregs.
claims.source: A promising candidate for an ESP-based therapeutic is the TGF-β mimic from the murine helminth parasite Heligmosomoides polygyrus (Hp-TGM). This molecule, which mimics endogenous proteins, exhibits potent immunoregulatory properties, including the expansion of Tregs (Johnston et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Johnston et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Intranasal and parenteral administration of Hp-TGM has successfully alleviated allergic airway inflammation in mice.
claims.source: Interestingly, intranasal and parenteral administration of Hp-TGM has successfully alleviated allergic airway inflammation in mice, demonstrating its capacity to control lung inflammation and allergic pathology (Chauché et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chauché et al., 2022, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: ESP contains EVs, allowing the helminth to deliver fragile cargo, like RNA, to distant cells.
claims.source: More recently, a paradigm shift occurred after discovering that ESP contains EVs, allowing the helminth to deliver fragile cargo, like RNA, to distant cells (Marcilla et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Marcilla et al., 2012.

claims.claim: Preimmunization with eggs of Schistosoma mansoni decreased immune cell infiltration into the central nervous system and improved clinical scores in EAE mice, with these effects being dependent on STAT6.
claims.source: Preimmunization with eggs of the trematode Schistosoma mansoni decreased immune cell infiltration into the central nervous system and improved clinical scores, with these effects being dependent on STAT6, a key mediator in Th2 differentiation (Sewell et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sewell et al., 2003, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: EAE disease severity was ameliorated by H. polygyrus in an IL-4Rα-dependent manner, and that protection requires live helminth infection.
claims.source: EAE disease severity was also ameliorated by H. polygyrus, in an IL-4Rα-dependent manner, and that protection requires live helminth infection.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data from EAE studies.

claims.claim: Hp-TGM does not fully replicate the suppressive effects of live H. polygyrus infection indicating that additional regulatory pathways are activated by infection.
claims.source: It is essential to note that Hp-TGM does not fully replicate the suppressive effects of live H. polygyrus infection indicating that additional regulatory pathways are activated by infection, which could be crucial for EAE (White et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to White et al., 2020, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: In the EAE model, disease protection by H. polygyrus is associated with increased Tregs, GATA3+, and ST2+ cells, reduced RORγt+ and IL-17A cell responses, and a lower level of myeloid cell infiltration into the CNS.
claims.source: In this model, disease protection is associated with increased Tregs, GATA3 +, and ST2 + cells, reduced RORγt+and IL-17A cell responses, and a lower level of myeloid cell infiltration into the CNS (White et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to White et al., 2020, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: Infection with Strongyloides venezuelensis on the development of EAE in mice found no alterations in clinical score or inflammation in the central nervous system.
claims.source: In contrast, another study analyzed the effects of infection with the nematode Strongyloides venezuelensis on the development of EAE in mice and found no alterations in clinical score or inflammation in the central nervous system (Chiuso-Minicucci et al., 2011)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chiuso-Minicucci et al., 2011, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: Infection with Toxocara canis worsened the course of EAE disease, resulting in higher clinical scores and increased weight loss.
claims.source: whereas infection with the nematode Toxocara canis worsened the course of the disease, resulting in higher clinical scores and increased weight loss (Novák et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Novák et al., 2022, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: MS patients with naturally-acquired gastrointestinal helminth infections showed a significantly lower number of relapses, reduced disability scores, and lower MRI activity compared to uninfected MS patients.
claims.source: Previously, pioneer work in the field studied a cohort of patients with MS in Argentina with naturally-acquired gastrointestinal helminth infections were followed for 5 y and showed a significantly lower number of relapses, reduced disability scores, and lower Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) activity compared to uninfected MS patients.
claims.evidence: This is presented as data from a longitudinal cohort study.

claims.claim: When four MS patients with helminth infections received anthelmintic treatment, their disability scores and their exacerbations significantly increased.
claims.source: Notably, when four of these patients received anthelmintic treatment, their disability scores and their exacerbations significantly increased, providing a direct role of the helminths in the modulation of this autoimmune disease (Correale and Farez, 2007; Correale and Farez, 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Correale and Farez, 2007; Correale and Farez, 2011) and provides data from patient observations.

claims.claim: Natural helminth infections enhanced a negative regulatory axis involving TAM receptors and their ligands, contributing to the dampening of the inflammatory response in MS patients.
claims.source: Furthermore, our group demonstrated that these natural helminth infections enhanced a negative regulatory axis, as the tyrosine kinase TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK (TAM) receptors and their ligands (PROS1 and GAS6), contributing to the dampening of the inflammatory response in patients with MS (Ortiz Wilczyñski et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ortiz Wilczyñski et al., 2020, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: MS patients showed reduced levels of TYRO3 in circulating monocytes, dendritic cells, and CD4 lymphocytes compared to healthy donors.
claims.source: In this study, we found first a reduced levels of TYRO3 in circulating monocytes, dendritic cells, and CD4 lymphocytes in patients with only MS, compared to healthy donors, denoting a strong influence of the disease condition.
claims.evidence: This is presented as data from the study.

claims.claim: MS patients with naturally acquired gastrointestinal helminth infections showed increased expression of three TAM receptors in antigen-presenting cells and their agonist GAS6 in circulating monocytes and CD4+ T cells compared to uninfected MS counterparts.
claims.source: Remarkably, this scenario is reversed in patients with MS who have naturally acquired gastrointestinal helminth infections, increasing the expression of three TAM receptors in antigen-presenting cells and their agonist GAS6 in circulating monocytes and CD4 + T cells compared to uninfected MS counterparts.
claims.evidence: This is presented as data from the study.

claims.claim: CD4+ IL-10+-producing cells from MS patients with helminthic infection showed higher levels of GAS6 expression than Th17 cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, CD4 + IL-10+-producing cells from MS patients with helminthic infection showed higher levels of GAS6 expression than Th17 cells, and GAS6 blockade induced an expansion of Th17 effector genes.
claims.evidence: This is presented as data from the study.

claims.claim: Adding recombinant GAS6 into activated CD4+ T cells from MS patients restrains the Th17 gene expression signature.
claims.source: Furthermore, adding recombinant GAS6 into activated CD4 + T cells from MS patients restrains the Th17 gene expression signature.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data.

claims.claim: The helminth-type 2 environment along with parasite-derived products may be training innate and adaptive immune cells as well as bone marrow precursors.
claims.source: Altogether, we can speculate here that the helminth-type 2 environment along with parasite-derived products, may be training innate and adaptive immune cells as well as bone marrow precursors.
claims.evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claims.claim: Almost 20 years of human clinical trials have explored the use of experimental helminth infections to treat inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, with some trials establishing that therapy is safe with some evidence of therapeutic effect.
claims.source: Almost 20 y of human clinical trials have explored the use of experimental helminth infections to treat inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, including celiac disease, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), MS, rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and psoriasis, based on their masterful skill to modulate immune responses. Thus far, some of these trials have established that therapy is safe with some evidence of therapeutic effect (Ryan et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ryan et al., 2020, which reviews clinical trial data.

claims.claim: Macrophages trained in vitro with Fasciola hepatica total extract (FHTE) exhibited increased production of IL-10 and IL-1RA while concomitantly decreasing the production of TNF and IL-12p40.
claims.source: Macrophages trained in vitro with Fasciola hepatica total extract (FHTE) exhibited increased production of the anti-inflammatory cytokines IL-10 and IL-1RA while concomitantly decreasing the production of the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF and IL-12p40 (Murphy et al., 2021; Quinn et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Murphy et al., 2021; Quinn et al., 2019), which provide experimental data.

claims.claim: Soluble products from Trichuris suis (TSP) induce a trained phenotype on bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) that restrains inflammatory responses.
claims.source: Zakeri et al., 2022 demonstrated that soluble products from the nematode Trichuris suis (TSP) induce a trained phenotype on bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) that restrains inflammatory responses.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zakeri et al., 2022, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: Treatment of BMDMs with TSP for 24 hr and subsequent stimulation with TLR agonists after 72 hr increased IL-10 secretion compared with untreated BMDMs.
claims.source: Treatment of BMDMs with TSP for 24 hr and subsequent stimulation with TLR agonists after 72 hr increased IL-10 secretion compared with untreated BMDMs.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data from the study.

claims.claim: TSP-treated BMDMs had a higher mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate, indicating increased oxidative phosphorylation than untreated BMDMs.
claims.source: Metabolic flux analyses revealed that TSP-treated BMDMs had a higher mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate, indicating increased oxidative phosphorylation than untreated BMDMs.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data from metabolic analyses.

claims.claim: FhHDM-1 could reverse the inflammatory trained phenotype of BMDMs from non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice.
claims.source: Interestingly, Quinteros et al. demonstrated that a peptide derived from the trematode Fasciola hepatica, FhHDM-1, could reverse the inflammatory trained phenotype of BMDMs from non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice (Quinteros et al., 2024).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Quinteros et al., 2024, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: BMDMs from NOD mice showed epigenetic signatures of trained immunity, as well as high glycolytic activity and enhanced secretion of IL-6 and TNF in response to LPS when compared to BMDMs from control mice.
claims.source: BMDMs from NOD mice showed epigenetic signatures of trained immunity, as well as high glycolytic activity and enhanced secretion of IL-6 and TNF in response to LPS when compared to BMDMs from control mice, suggesting that progenitor cells in the bone marrow of NOD mice had immune training.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data with an inference about bone marrow progenitor cells.

claims.claim: Administration of intraperitoneal injections of FhHDM-1 reduced glycolytic activity in BMDMs from NOD mice in response to LPS.
claims.source: Administration of intraperitoneal injections of FhHDM-1 and posterior analysis of BMDMs revealed a reduction in glycolytic activity in response to LPS in contrast to NOD mice not treated with the helminth product.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data.

claims.claim: Treating mice with F. hepatica ESP induces an anti-inflammatory phenotype in bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells.
claims.source: Their research demonstrated that treating mice with F. hepatica ESP induces an anti-inflammatory phenotype in bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells (HSC).
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data from research by Mills and colleagues.

claims.claim: F. hepatica ESP treatment leads to an expansion of the peripheral population of Ly6Clow monocytes, associated with anti-inflammatory activity.
claims.source: This, in turn, leads to an expansion of the peripheral population of Ly6Clow monocytes, associated with anti-inflammatory activity, and the generation of BMDMs that secrete more anti-inflammatory cytokines and less pro-inflammatory cytokines after stimulation with various TLR agonists.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data.

claims.claim: F. hepatica ESP provides protection against EAE through the generation of anti-inflammatory monocytes that suppress T-cell mediated autoimmunity, and this effect persists for at least 8 months.
claims.source: More importantly, this mechanism provides protection against EAE through the generation of anti-inflammatory monocytes that suppress T-cell mediated autoimmunity, and this effect persists for at least 8 mo (Cunningham et al., 2021), see also Figure 2.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cunningham et al., 2021 and reference to Figure 2, providing experimental data.

claims.claim: Infection by Strongyloides venezuelensis induced resistance to a subsequent infection by Nippostrongylus brasiliensis through innate cell-dependent mechanisms in mice.
claims.source: Trained immunity in Th2 responses has also been studied, and Yasuda et al. found that infection by the nematode Strongyloides venezuelensis induced resistance to a subsequent infection by Nippostrongylus brasiliensis, an unrelated nematode, through innate cell-dependent mechanisms in mice (Yasuda et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yasuda et al., 2018, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: The protective effect of S. venezuelensis infection lasted at least 3 months and was mediated by training ILC2s in the lung.
claims.source: This effect lasted at least 3 mo and was mediated by training ILC2s in the lung, a tissue through which the larvae migrate.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data.

claims.claim: In vitro stimulation with PMA and ionomycin led to enhanced production of IL-5 and IL-13 in ILC2s derived from mice that had been infected with S. venezuelensis.
claims.source: In vitro stimulation of these cells with PMA and ionomycin, two potent cell activators, led to enhanced production of the cytokines IL-5 and IL-13 in ILC2s derived from mice that had been infected with S. venezuelensis.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data.

claims.claim: After infection with N. brasiliensis, the expression of Il13 and Irf4 mRNAs was significantly higher in ILC2s from mice that had been previously infected with S. venezuelensis compared to uninfected mice.
claims.source: After the infection with N. brasiliensis, the expression of Il13 and Irf4 mRNAs was significantly higher in ILC2s from mice that had been previously infected with S. venezuelensis compared to uninfected mice.
claims.evidence: This is presented as experimental data.

claims.claim: Helminths induce a systemic innate mucin response that primes peripheral barrier sites for protection against subsequent secondary helminth infections.
claims.source: Furthermore, helminths induce a systemic innate mucin response that primes peripheral barrier sites for protection against subsequent secondary helminth infections.
claims.evidence: This is presented as a general finding from research.

claims.claim: Intestinal helminths (Trichinella spiralis or Heligmosomoides polygyrus) may protect their hosts against co-infection by N. brasiliensis at a distal site via ILC2s in the gut and circulation of activated CD4+ T cells.
claims.source: Mechanistically, a cross-mucosal immune mechanism by which intestinal helminths (Trichinella spiralis or Heligmosomoides polygyrus) may protect their hosts against co-infection by a different parasite (N. brasiliensis) at a distal site via ILC2s in the gut and circulation of activated CD4 + T cells that can be triggered to release effector cytokines and mount inflammatory responses by tissue damage-associated alarmins, such as IL-33 priming (Campbell et al., 2019; Filbey et al., 2019; Löser et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Campbell et al., 2019; Filbey et al., 2019; Löser et al., 2019), which provide experimental data.

claims.claim: EVs influence a wide range of biological systems, including mammalian immunity, and emerging evidence suggests they play a role in immune regulation.
claims.source: EVs influence a wide range of biological systems, including mammalian immunity, and emerging evidence suggests they play a role in immune regulation (Kalluri and LeBleu, 2020; Zhou et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Kalluri and LeBleu, 2020; Zhou et al., 2020).

claims.claim: The malaria parasite, Plasmodium berghei, secretes EVs that can inhibit T-cell responses.
claims.source: The malaria parasite, Plasmodium berghei, secretes EVs that can inhibit T-cell responses (Demarta-Gatsi et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Demarta-Gatsi et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Leishmania donovani exosomes have been found to push monocytes and dendritic cells towards anti-inflammatory phenotypes, increasing Th2 polarisation.
claims.source: Leishmania donovani exosomes have been found to push monocytes and dendritic cells towards anti-inflammatory phenotypes, increasing Th2 polarisation and thereby contributing to the disease (Silverman et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Silverman et al., 2010.

claims.claim: The composition of helminth-derived EVs varies depending on the gender and life cycle stage of the parasite.
claims.source: The composition of helminth-derived EVs varies depending on the gender and life cycle stage of the parasite.
claims.evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about helminth EVs.

claims.claim: Helminth EVs contain various small RNA species, particularly microRNAs (miRNAs), which have been implicated in host-helminth interactions.
claims.source: However, helminth EVs also contain various small RNA species, particularly microRNAs (miRNAs), which have been implicated in host-helminth interactions and provide some of the most significant clues for immunomodulation (Sotillo et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2018; Fromm et al., 2017; Hansen et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Sotillo et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2018; Fromm et al., 2017; Hansen et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2020).

claims.claim: Lipids can possess bioactivity, directly influencing cell uptake and modulating immune responses.
claims.source: Lipids can possess bioactivity, directly influencing cell uptake and modulating immune responses (Assunção et al., 2017; Magalhães et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Assunção et al., 2017; Magalhães et al., 2018).

claims.claim: Glycans have been identified as key players in the regulation of EV uptake, affecting the cell tropism of EVs.
claims.source: Glycans have been identified as key players in the regulation of EV uptake, affecting the cell tropism of EVs. Glycans may even play a role in the biodistribution of helminth EVs (Drurey and Maizels, 2021; Whitehead et al., 2020; de la Torre-Escudero et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Drurey and Maizels, 2021; Whitehead et al., 2020; de la Torre-Escudero et al., 2019).

claims.claim: Trained immunity may originate at the hematopoietic stem cell stage.
claims.source: Intriguingly, recent studies suggest that trained immunity may even originate at the hematopoietic stem cell stage, (Quinn et al., 2019; Cunningham et al., 2021), see also Figure 2.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Quinn et al., 2019; Cunningham et al., 2021) and reference to Figure 2.

claims.claim: Helminths can promote tissue infiltration by releasing cathepsins and other proteases.
claims.source: Additionally, helminths can promote tissue infiltration by releasing cathepsins and other proteases.
claims.evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about helminth biology.

claims.claim: The migration of hookworm larvae through the lung causes significant mechanical and enzymatic damage, but rapid tissue repair is observed, potentially facilitated by EVs to restore homeostasis.
claims.source: Similarly, the migration of hookworm larvae through the lung causes significant mechanical and enzymatic damage, but rapid tissue repair is observed, potentially facilitated by EVs to restore homeostasis (Drurey and Maizels, 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Drurey and Maizels, 2021 and includes speculation about the role of EVs.

claims.claim: Tuft cells have been identified in intestinal and lung tissues as rare chemosensory epithelial cells that monitor their environment and relay messages to the surrounding tissue via secretion of neuro- and immunomodulatory molecules.
claims.source: Tuft cells have been identified in intestinal and lung tissues (Haber et al., 2017) as rare chemosensory epithelial cells that monitor their environment and relay messages to the surrounding tissue via secretion of neuro- and immunomodulatory molecules (Strine and Wilen, 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Haber et al., 2017; Strine and Wilen, 2022).

claims.claim: Tuft cells have been linked to the establishment of T cell tolerance, cross-talk with the nervous system, and epithelial repair and remodeling.
claims.source: Based on their known signaling pathways, tuft cells have been linked to a wide variety of bodily functions, such as the establishment of T cell tolerance (Miller et al., 2018), cross-talk with the nervous system (Matsumoto et al., 2011), and epithelial repair and remodeling (Huang et al., 2024).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Miller et al., 2018; Matsumoto et al., 2011; Huang et al., 2024).

claims.claim: Tuft cells have been implicated in IBD as well as contributing to helminth clearance by activation of the tuft-ILC2 circuit.
claims.source: Given these roles, it is unsurprising that tuft cells have been implicated in IBD as well as contributing to helminth clearance by activation of the tuft-ILC2 circuit that results in rapid remodeling of the intestinal epithelium, and protective functions of IBD manifestations (Yi et al., 2019; Kjærgaard et al., 2021; Qu et al., 2015; Banerjee et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Yi et al., 2019; Kjærgaard et al., 2021; Qu et al., 2015; Banerjee et al., 2020).

claims.claim: Trained immunity of intestinal tuft cells during infancy enhances host defense against enteroviral infections in mice.
claims.source: In this sense, an interesting work by Chen et al., 2024 showed that trained immunity of intestinal tuft cells during infancy enhances host defense against enteroviral infections in mice.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2024, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: Tuft cells can be trained by IL-25, which supports faster and higher levels of IL-25 production in response to enteroviral infection and exhibits an anti-enteroviral effect.
claims.source: The authors showed that tuft cells can be trained by IL-25, which supports faster and higher levels of IL-25 production in response to enteroviral infection and further exhibits an anti-enteroviral effect (Chen et al., 2024).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2024, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: BCG vaccination has been shown to reprogram hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) at the transcriptomic, epigenetic, and functional levels, generating trained monocytes for at least 3 months.
claims.source: For example, BCG vaccination has been shown to reprogram hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) at the transcriptomic, epigenetic, and functional levels, generating trained monocytes for at least 3 mo (Cirovic et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2024).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Cirovic et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2024), which provide experimental data.

claims.claim: There are over 80 recognized autoimmune diseases, including IBD, MS, RA, and type 1 diabetes.
claims.source: With over 80 recognized autoimmune diseases, including IBD, MS, RA, and type 1 diabetes (T1D), the global health (10%) and economic burden is immense.
claims.evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about autoimmune diseases.

claims.claim: Type 2 immune responses play a crucial role in protecting against metazoan endo- and ectoparasites, regulating metabolism, and promoting tissue repair.
claims.source: Type 2 immune responses, rooted in ancient defense mechanisms, play a crucial role in protecting against metazoan endo- and ectoparasites, regulating metabolism, and promoting tissue repair.
claims.evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about type 2 immunity.

claims.claim: Dysregulation of type 2 immune responses can lead to allergic disorders, impaired tissue healing, and metabolic disturbances.
claims.source: While these responses are essential for health, dysregulation can lead to allergic disorders, impaired tissue healing, and metabolic disturbances (Maizels and Gause, 2023; Gause et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Maizels and Gause, 2023; Gause et al., 2013).

claims.claim: The adaptation of the developing immune system to the presence of helminths was largely epigenetic and was lost after a few generations without them.
claims.source: It was once logical to postulate evolved dependence on helminths in the past (Bilbo et al., 2011; Maizels, 2020); however, it now seems more likely that the adaptation of the developing immune system to the presence of helminths was largely epigenetic and was lost after a few generations without them.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Bilbo et al., 2011; Maizels, 2020) and represents a hypothesis.

claims.claim: Clinical trials may not yield helpful results until we can precisely identify the optimal combination of patient characteristics, genetic factors, disease stage, and specific helminth species, ESPs, or metabolic byproducts for effectively training the immune system.
claims.source: These reversible epigenetic mechanisms help us to understand the conflicting and disappointing results of helminth therapy trials. Clinical trials may not yield helpful results, and face significant challenges until we can precisely identify the optimal combination of patient characteristics, genetic factors, disease stage, and specific helminth species, ESPs, or metabolic byproducts for effectively train immune system (Rook, 2023; Smallwood et al., 2017; Ryan et al., 2020; Loke et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Rook, 2023; Smallwood et al., 2017; Ryan et al., 2020; Loke et al., 2022) and represents an inference about clinical trial challenges.

claims.claim: Several animal models have shown the beneficial effect of helminth infections or their products on the microbiota and the immune regulation of IBD.
claims.source: Several animal models have shown the beneficial effect of helminth infections or their products on the microbiota and the immune regulation of IBD (Atagozli et al., 2023; Shi et al., 2022; Ryan et al., 2022; Rapin et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Atagozli et al., 2023; Shi et al., 2022; Ryan et al., 2022; Rapin et al., 2020).

claims.claim: IBD-associated dysbiosis is marked by a loss of beneficial Bacteroides and Firmicutes and an increase in pro-inflammatory Enterobacteriaceae.
claims.source: Thus, IBD-associated dysbiosis, marked by a loss of beneficial Bacteroides and Firmicutes and an increase in pro-inflammatory Enterobacteriaceae, is a key feature of the disease.
claims.evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about IBD.

claims.claim: A novel discovery and validation pipeline led to the identification of numerous anti-inflammatory biologics from the recombinant secretome of gut-dwelling hookworms that demonstrated protective effects against inducible colitis in mice.
claims.source: A novel discovery and validation pipeline, detailed by Ryan et al., 2022, led to the identification of numerous anti-inflammatory biologics from the recombinant secretome of gut-dwelling hookworms. These proteins, representing distinct families, demonstrated protective effects against inducible colitis in mice, suggesting they are safe and promising drug candidates.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ryan et al., 2022, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: Deworming trials have revealed an increased likelihood of developing various autoimmune and metabolic diseases with the use of antihelminthic drugs.
claims.source: Deworming trials have revealed an increased likelihood of developing various autoimmune and metabolic diseases with the use of antihelminthic drugs. This underscores the importance of considering the evolutionary context of human-parasite interactions and the potential risks of disrupting these ancient relationships (Tahapary et al., 2017; Sanya et al., 2020; Flohr et al., 2010; Shute et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Tahapary et al., 2017; Sanya et al., 2020; Flohr et al., 2010; Shute et al., 2021).

claims.claim: Bacterial SCFAs via free fatty-acid receptor-2 (ffar2) play a critical role in H. diminuta-induced colitis improvement, with IL-10 being necessary for upregulating SCFA transporters/receptors, and butyrate regulating IL-10 receptor expression.
claims.source: In this sense, Shute et al., 2021 demonstrates the critical role of bacterial SCFAs via free fatty-acid receptor-2 (ffar2) in H. diminuta-induced colitis improvement, the necessity of IL-10 in upregulating SCFA transporters/receptors, and butyrate's regulation of IL-10 receptor expression.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shute et al., 2021, which provides experimental data.

claims.claim: The failure of helminth therapy in some IBD trials may be due to patient-specific deficiencies in SCFA production, transport, or IL-10 signaling.
claims.source: The findings suggest that the failure of helminth therapy in some IBD trials may be due to patient-specific deficiencies in SCFA production, transport, or IL-10 signaling.
claims.evidence: This is presented as an inference from the findings.

claims.claim: Helminth therapy was safe and tolerable in IBD clinical trials.
claims.source: Despite this, helminth therapy was safe and tolerable (Ryan et al., 2020; Alghanmi et al., 2024; Shields and Cooper, 2022; Axelrad et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Ryan et al., 2020; Alghanmi et al., 2024; Shields and Cooper, 2022; Axelrad et al., 2021) from systematic reviews.

claims.claim: MS prevalence rates are increased in high-latitude regions yet uncommon near the equator.
claims.source: One of the most striking illustrations of the importance of the environment in MS pathogenesis is its geographic distribution; prevalence rates are increased in high-latitude regions yet uncommon near the equator (Melcon et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Melcon et al., 2014 and represents established epidemiological knowledge.

claims.claim: The gut biome is recognized as a critical regulator of immune and nervous system function, significantly impacting both the onset and progression of MS.
claims.source: The gut biome is recognized as a critical regulator of immune and nervous system function, significantly impacting both the onset and progression of MS. It may contribute to and influence the production of soluble metabolites and immune and neuroendocrine factors (Correale et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Correale et al., 2022.

claims.claim: The treatment of relapsing MS patients with larvae of Necator americanus was proved to be safe and well tolerated and induced a significant increase in peripheral blood Tregs, but the number of new/enlarged brain lesions was not different from the placebo group.
claims.source: The treatment of relapsing MS patients with larvae of the nematode Necator americanus was proved to be safe and well tolerated and induced a significant increase in peripheral blood Tregs. Still, the number of new/enlarged brain lesions was not different from the placebo group (Tanasescu et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tanasescu et al., 2020, which provides clinical trial data.

claims.claim: MS patients tolerated Trichuris suis egg infection, but it didn't show beneficial effects.
claims.source: Similarly, results were obtained using eggs from the nematode Trichuris suis, where MS patients tolerated the helminth infection, but it didn't show beneficial effects (Voldsgaard et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Voldsgaard et al., 2015, which provides clinical trial data.

claims.claim: MS patients receiving TSO treatment established a T. suis-specific T- and B-cell response with varying degrees of T cell responses and cellular functionality across individuals.
claims.source: In other recent study, MS patients receiving TSO treatment established a T. suis-specific T- and B-cell response; however, with varying degrees of T cell responses and cellular functionality across individuals, which might account for the overall miscellaneous clinical efficacy in the studied patients (Yordanova et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yordanova et al., 2021, which provides clinical trial data.

claims.claim: The escalating global prevalence of asthma and allergic airway inflammation (20%) is a consequence of complex gene-environment interactions that modulate the immune system, and are strongly linked to modern westernized lifestyles.
claims.source: The escalating global prevalence of these conditions (20%) is a consequence of complex gene-environment interactions that modulate the immune system, and are strongly linked to modern westernized lifestyles (Murrison et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Murrison et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Several ESP derived from different helminth species have been shown to reduce or suppress allergic airway eosinophilia and inflammation in mice.
claims.source: Moreover, several ESP derived from different helminth species have been shown to reduce or suppress allergic airway eosinophilia and inflammation in mice (Chauché et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2019; Pitrez et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2025).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Chauché et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2019; Pitrez et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2025), which provide experimental data.

claims.claim: Some studies have shown an exacerbation of allergic asthma in response to the administration of helminth antigens.
claims.source: However, other studies have shown an exacerbation of allergic asthma in response to the administration of helminth antigens, unveiling the complexity of the interaction between these type 2 immunity inducers (Ghabdian et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ghabdian et al., 2022.

claims.claim: Epidemiological data suggests an inverse correlation between helminth infections and those of asthma and allergy.
claims.source: As seen with autoimmune diseases, epidemiological data suggests an inverse correlation between helminth infections and those of asthma and allergy (Logan et al., 2018)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Logan et al., 2018.

claims.claim: A. lumbricoides has been associated with an increased risk of asthma and disease severity.
claims.source: however, when considering the parasite species, some like A. lumbricoides have been associated with an increased risk of asthma and disease severity (Cruz et al., 2017; Arrais et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Cruz et al., 2017; Arrais et al., 2022).

claims.claim: Clinical trials using N. americanus and T. suis ova for asthma and allergic rhinitis were proven to be safe and well tolerated, but clinical benefits were minimal.
claims.source: Clinical trials have been conducted to assess the efficacy of helminth therapy for asthma and allergic rhinitis, using N. americanus and T. suis ova, respectively. Even though they were proven to be safe and well tolerated, clinical benefits were minimal.
claims.evidence: This is presented as a summary of clinical trial outcomes.

claims.claim: It is speculated that the discrepancy between human and animal studies could be explained by the fact that helminths are effective at preventing the development of allergy, not treating it.
claims.source: It is speculated that the discrepancy between human and animal studies could be explained by the fact that helminths are effective at preventing the development of allergy, not treating it (Evans and Mitre, 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Evans and Mitre, 2015 and is explicitly stated as speculation.

claims.claim: There is an inverse relationship observed between human helminth infection, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes.
claims.source: There is an inverse relationship observed between human helminth infection, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes, and it has been proposed that chronic helminth infection results in long-term beneficial effects on host metabolism, especially on white adipose tissue, intestines, and liver (van der Zande et al., 2019; Wiria et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (van der Zande et al., 2019; Wiria et al., 2014).

claims.claim: The successful application of helminth therapy may ultimately depend on precise patient selection and the careful matching of specific helminth species.
claims.source: In developed countries, the successful application of helminth therapy may ultimately depend on precise patient selection and the careful matching of specific helminth species (Rook, 2023; Smallwood et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations (Rook, 2023; Smallwood et al., 2017) and represents an inference about future therapeutic approaches.

claims.claim: The identification and characterization of helminth molecules and vesicles and the molecular pathways they target in the host represent the most valuable opportunity to develop tailored drugs inspired by nature.
claims.source: Furthermore, the identification and characterization of helminth molecules and vesicles and the molecular pathways they target in the host represent the most valuable opportunity to develop tailored drugs inspired by nature that are efficacious, safe, and have minimal immunogenicity (Maizels and Gause, 2023; Maizels et al., 2018; Ryan et al., 2020; Drurey and Maizels, 2021), Figure 3.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Maizels and Gause, 2023; Maizels et al., 2018; Ryan et al., 2020; Drurey and Maizels, 2021) and reference to Figure 3.

claims.claim: Efforts to mimic the natural delivery of helminth miRNAs via EVs using synthetic exosomes could revolutionize miRNA-based therapies.
claims.source: The natural delivery of helminth miRNAs via EVs is a particularly intriguing strategy, and efforts to mimic this process using synthetic exosomes could revolutionize miRNA-based therapies (Ryan et al., 2020), see Figure 3.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ryan et al., 2020 and reference to Figure 3, and represents speculation about future therapeutic approaches.

results.result: Trained immunity is a long-term functional reprogramming of innate immune mechanisms that can be induced by environmental stimuli through metabolic or epigenetic changes. This concept challenges the traditional view that immunological memory is exclusive to adaptive immunity, as most species rely solely on innate immunity for host defense.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 provide a coherent definition and evolutionary rationale for trained immunity. C1 defines the concept with citation support (Netea et al., 2020), C2 establishes that most species lack adaptive immunity, and C3 logically infers that immunological memory must exist in innate immunity across organisms (supported by Divangahi et al., 2021). The claims are internally consistent and well-supported by citations.

results.result: BCG vaccination and various infections induce trained immunity that provides heterologous protection against unrelated pathogens in both animal models and humans. This protection operates through T cell-independent mechanisms involving innate immune cells like macrophages.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C8 collectively demonstrate trained immunity across multiple experimental systems with strong citation support. Animal studies (C4, C7, C8) and human trials (C5) show BCG and infection-induced protection against diverse pathogens. Epidemiological data (C6) further supports heterologous vaccine effects. The mechanistic details (IFNγ production, macrophage activation) strengthen the evidence.

results.result: Trained immunity can have both beneficial and detrimental effects depending on context. While it may contribute to pathophysiology of cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases, it can also enhance immune self-tolerance in autoimmune conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C11 present a balanced view of trained immunity's dual nature. C9 and C10 demonstrate maladaptive effects (supported by Christ et al., 2018), while C11 shows beneficial effects in autoimmunity models (Ristori et al., 2018). The claims are well-cited and acknowledge the context-dependent nature of trained immunity, though C9 is appropriately marked as speculative.

results.result: The gut microbiome, established through coevolution with humans, plays an essential role in immune system development and training. Dysbiosis and early-life disturbances in microbiome composition are associated with inflammatory diseases, while a healthy microbiome is characterized by high diversity and evenness.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C17 establish the importance of the gut microbiome in immune regulation with strong citation support. The claims progress logically from the symbiotic relationship (C12) through dysbiosis effects (C13-C15) to characteristics of healthy microbiomes (C16-C17). Multiple citations support each claim, and the functional niche concept (C17) provides mechanistic insight.

results.result: The rise in inflammatory and autoimmune diseases in industrialized societies is explained by the 'old friends hypothesis,' which posits that lack of exposure to co-evolved organisms leads to immune dysregulation. This represents an evolutionary mismatch between modern environments and immune system development.
results.evaluation: Claims C18-C21 present a well-supported epidemiological and theoretical framework. C18 and C19 establish the epidemiological pattern with citations, C20 introduces the 'old friends hypothesis' with appropriate attribution and citations, and C21 extends this to the evolutionary mismatch concept. The progression is logical and well-documented, though C21 appropriately includes speculation.

results.result: While genetics plays an important role in autoimmune disease predisposition, the rapid rise in autoimmune diseases cannot be explained by genetic changes alone, indicating that environmental factors are decisive.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C23 present a logical argument about the etiology of autoimmune diseases. C22 establishes genetic contribution with citations, while C23 makes a valid inference that the speed of the 'autoimmune epidemic' requires environmental explanations. The reasoning is sound and the inference is appropriately marked.

results.result: The microbiota maintains immune homeostasis through production of three major classes of metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan metabolites, and bile acid metabolites) that modulate immune responses through various receptors. Imbalances in these metabolites due to dysbiosis are associated with inflammatory diseases.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C29 provide a comprehensive and well-cited mechanistic explanation of microbiota-immune interactions. Each metabolite class is described with specific receptors and functions (C25-C28), and the clinical relevance is established (C29). The claims are supported by appropriate citations and Figure 1 provides visual support for C26.

results.result: Helminth infections are associated with changes in microbiome composition, including increased abundance of anti-inflammatory bacteria like Faecalibacterium and overall increased microbial diversity, though results vary across studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C32 present specific observational data from human studies with appropriate citations (Gordon et al., 2020; Tee et al., 2022). C31 provides functional context for Faecalibacterium. The claims acknowledge variability in results, which is scientifically appropriate. The data are from specific populations but are well-documented.

results.result: Helminth infections induce both type 2 immunity for parasite expulsion and immunoregulatory pathways for chronic infection establishment. The balance between Th2 and Treg responses is essential for host-parasite survival, and helminths can modulate immunity through microbiome changes.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C36 describe the complex immune response to helminths with strong citation support. C33 and C34 establish the dual nature of the response (well-cited established knowledge), C35 provides evolutionary reasoning (appropriately marked as inference), and C36 gives a specific mechanistic example with experimental data (Wang et al., 2023a).

results.result: Helminth excretory/secretory products (ESP) comprise diverse molecules including proteins, peptides, enzymes, lipids, glycans, and EVs. Specific ESP molecules like Hp-TGM show immunoregulatory properties and therapeutic potential in mouse models of allergic inflammation.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C40 describe ESP composition and therapeutic potential with appropriate citations. C37 defines ESP comprehensively, C38-C39 provide a specific example (Hp-TGM) with experimental validation in mice, and C40 introduces the paradigm shift of EV-mediated delivery. All claims are well-supported by citations.

results.result: Helminth effects on EAE (a mouse model of MS) are species-specific and complex. While S. mansoni eggs and H. polygyrus ameliorate disease through STAT6/IL-4Rα-dependent mechanisms involving Tregs and reduced Th17 responses, S. venezuelensis shows no effect and T. canis worsens disease.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C46 present a comprehensive view of helminth effects in EAE with appropriate citations for each study. The claims acknowledge both positive (C41-C44), neutral (C45), and negative (C46) effects, demonstrating scientific rigor. C43 appropriately notes that Hp-TGM doesn't fully replicate live infection effects. The mechanistic details in C44 are well-supported.

results.result: MS patients with naturally-acquired helminth infections show reduced disease activity, and anthelmintic treatment worsens outcomes. Helminth infections enhance TAM receptor signaling and GAS6 expression, which dampens inflammatory responses by restraining Th17 differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C53 present compelling observational and mechanistic data from human MS patients. The longitudinal cohort data (C47-C48) provides strong evidence for helminth effects, and the mechanistic studies (C49-C53) identify specific pathways. The experimental validation with recombinant GAS6 (C53) strengthens the mechanistic claims. All claims are appropriately cited or marked as data.

results.result: The helminth-type 2 environment and parasite-derived products may train innate and adaptive immune cells as well as bone marrow precursors.
results.evaluation: Claim C54 is explicitly marked as speculation and serves as a hypothesis connecting previous observations. While it's a reasonable inference based on the preceding data, it lacks direct experimental validation. The claim appropriately acknowledges its speculative nature.

results.result: Nearly 20 years of clinical trials have explored helminth therapy for inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, establishing safety with some evidence of therapeutic effect.
results.evaluation: Claim C55 provides a summary of clinical trial history with citation to a review (Ryan et al., 2020). The claim appropriately qualifies the therapeutic evidence as 'some evidence,' acknowledging mixed results. This is a reasonable summary statement supported by a comprehensive review.

results.result: Helminth products (FHTE and TSP) can train macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype in vitro, characterized by increased IL-10 and IL-1RA production, decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines, and metabolic shifts toward oxidative phosphorylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C59 present in vitro experimental data demonstrating anti-inflammatory trained immunity. C56 and C57 establish the phenotype with appropriate citations, while C58-C59 provide specific experimental details including metabolic measurements. The data are internally consistent and well-documented.

results.result: The helminth-derived peptide FhHDM-1 can reverse inflammatory trained immunity in NOD mice, reducing glycolytic activity and pro-inflammatory cytokine production in bone marrow-derived macrophages.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C62 present a coherent experimental story with citation support (Quinteros et al., 2024). C61 establishes the baseline inflammatory phenotype in NOD mice (with appropriate inference about bone marrow progenitors), and C62 demonstrates reversal by FhHDM-1. The metabolic and cytokine data are consistent with anti-inflammatory training.

results.result: F. hepatica ESP induces central trained immunity by reprogramming bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells, leading to expansion of anti-inflammatory Ly6Clow monocytes and long-lasting protection against EAE (at least 8 months).
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C65 present a comprehensive mechanistic study with strong citation support (Cunningham et al., 2021) and Figure 2 reference. The claims demonstrate central training at the HSC level, peripheral effects on monocyte populations, and functional protection in disease models. The 8-month duration is particularly notable for demonstrating long-term effects.

results.result: S. venezuelensis infection induces trained immunity in lung ILC2s that provides cross-protection against N. brasiliensis infection for at least 3 months, characterized by enhanced IL-5 and IL-13 production and increased Il13 and Irf4 expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C69 describe trained immunity in type 2 responses with citation support (Yasuda et al., 2018). The claims provide cross-protection data (C66-C67), in vitro functional validation (C68), and molecular evidence (C69). This demonstrates that trained immunity extends beyond classical pro-inflammatory responses to include type 2 immunity.

results.result: Helminths induce systemic innate mucin responses that prime peripheral barrier sites for protection against secondary infections through cross-mucosal immune mechanisms involving ILC2s and CD4+ T cells activated by alarmins like IL-33.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C71 describe cross-mucosal protection mechanisms with strong citation support (Campbell et al., 2019; Filbey et al., 2019; Löser et al., 2019). The claims explain how intestinal helminths can protect against lung infections through systemic immune priming, providing mechanistic details about ILC2s and alarmin signaling.

results.result: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) from various pathogens, including parasites, play important roles in immune regulation by modulating T-cell responses and polarizing immune cells toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C74 establish the role of pathogen-derived EVs in immune modulation with appropriate citations. C72 provides the general framework, while C73-C74 give specific examples from malaria and Leishmania. The claims are well-supported but represent background information rather than novel findings from this manuscript.

results.result: Helminth-derived EVs contain diverse cargo including proteins, miRNAs, lipids, and glycans that vary by parasite gender and life stage. These components, particularly miRNAs and glycans, play important roles in host-helminth interactions and EV uptake.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C78 describe EV composition and function with appropriate citations. C75 establishes variability (presented as knowledge), C76 highlights miRNAs with multiple citations, and C77-C78 describe lipid and glycan functions. The claims are well-supported but primarily review existing knowledge rather than presenting new findings.

results.result: Trained immunity may originate at the hematopoietic stem cell stage.
results.evaluation: Claim C79 is supported by citations (Quinn et al., 2019; Cunningham et al., 2021) and Figure 2. While presented as a recent suggestion, this concept is supported by the experimental data described in claims C63-C65. The claim appropriately acknowledges this as an emerging concept.

results.result: Helminths promote tissue infiltration through protease release and cause tissue damage during migration, but rapid repair is observed, potentially facilitated by EVs.
results.evaluation: Claim C80 is presented as established knowledge without citation, while C81 includes speculation about EV involvement in tissue repair (appropriately marked). The tissue damage and repair observations are likely well-established, but the specific role of EVs in repair remains speculative and requires further validation.

results.result: Tuft cells are rare chemosensory epithelial cells in intestinal and lung tissues that regulate immune responses, establish T cell tolerance, communicate with the nervous system, and contribute to epithelial repair, helminth clearance, and IBD pathology.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C84 describe tuft cell biology and functions with appropriate citations for each function. The claims establish tuft cells as important immune regulators with diverse roles. All claims are well-supported by citations, though they primarily review existing knowledge about tuft cells.

results.result: Intestinal tuft cells can be trained by IL-25 during infancy, leading to enhanced IL-25 production and anti-enteroviral effects in response to subsequent enteroviral infections in mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C86 present novel experimental data about tuft cell trained immunity with citation support (Chen et al., 2024). The claims demonstrate that trained immunity extends to epithelial cells and can provide antiviral protection. This represents an important extension of trained immunity concepts.

results.result: BCG vaccination reprograms hematopoietic stem cells at transcriptomic, epigenetic, and functional levels, generating trained monocytes for at least 3 months.
results.evaluation: Claim C87 is well-supported by citations (Cirovic et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2024) and provides evidence for central trained immunity in humans. This is an important validation that trained immunity mechanisms observed in animal models also occur in humans, though the 3-month duration is shorter than some animal studies.

results.result: Over 80 autoimmune diseases affect global health significantly. Type 2 immune responses are essential for parasite defense, metabolism, and tissue repair, but dysregulation leads to allergic disorders and metabolic disturbances.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C90 provide background on autoimmune diseases and type 2 immunity with appropriate citations. C88 establishes the disease burden (presented as knowledge), while C89-C90 describe type 2 immunity functions and consequences of dysregulation (supported by Maizels and Gause, 2023; Gause et al., 2013). These are well-established concepts.

results.result: The adaptation of the immune system to helminths was likely epigenetic and reversible rather than genetic, explaining conflicting clinical trial results. Successful helminth therapy requires precise matching of patient characteristics, genetics, disease stage, and specific helminth products.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C92 present a hypothesis about epigenetic adaptation with citation support (Bilbo et al., 2011; Maizels, 2020; Rook, 2023; Smallwood et al., 2017; Ryan et al., 2020; Loke et al., 2022). C91 appropriately marks this as speculation, while C92 makes a reasonable inference about clinical trial requirements. The claims provide a framework for understanding trial failures.

results.result: Animal models demonstrate beneficial effects of helminth infections on IBD through microbiota modulation and immune regulation. A discovery pipeline identified anti-inflammatory proteins from hookworm secretome that protect against colitis in mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C95 describe animal model evidence for helminth therapy in IBD with appropriate citations. C93 and C94 establish the context, while C95 presents specific drug discovery work (Ryan et al., 2022). The claims are well-supported and demonstrate translational potential, though they are limited to animal models.

results.result: Deworming trials show increased risk of autoimmune and metabolic diseases. H. diminuta-induced colitis improvement requires bacterial SCFAs via ffar2 and IL-10 signaling, suggesting that helminth therapy failures may result from patient-specific deficiencies in these pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C98 present important mechanistic insights into helminth-microbiota-immune interactions. C96 establishes the risk of deworming with citations, C97 provides specific mechanistic data (Shute et al., 2021), and C98 makes a reasonable inference about trial failures. The claims are well-supported and provide actionable insights for future trials.

results.result: Helminth therapy was safe and tolerable in IBD clinical trials according to systematic reviews.
results.evaluation: Claim C99 is supported by multiple systematic review citations (Ryan et al., 2020; Alghanmi et al., 2024; Shields and Cooper, 2022; Axelrad et al., 2021). This is an important finding for translational potential, though efficacy remains uncertain. The claim appropriately focuses on safety rather than efficacy.

results.result: MS shows a striking geographic distribution with higher prevalence at high latitudes. The gut biome is recognized as a critical regulator of immune and nervous system function that impacts MS onset and progression.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C101 establish the environmental component of MS and the role of the gut biome with appropriate citations (Melcon et al., 2014; Correale et al., 2022). These claims provide important context for understanding helminth effects on MS, though they represent established knowledge rather than novel findings.

results.result: Clinical trials of helminth therapy in MS using N. americanus and T. suis showed safety and tolerability but failed to demonstrate clinical efficacy, despite inducing immune changes like increased Tregs and parasite-specific responses.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C104 present clinical trial data with appropriate citations (Tanasescu et al., 2020; Voldsgaard et al., 2015; Yordanova et al., 2021). The claims honestly report negative results while noting immune changes, demonstrating scientific rigor. The variability in individual responses (C104) may explain the lack of overall efficacy.

results.result: Asthma and allergic airway inflammation affect 20% of the global population and are linked to westernized lifestyles. Helminth ESPs reduce allergic inflammation in mouse models, but some studies show exacerbation, revealing complex interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C107 present the asthma context and experimental evidence with appropriate citations. C105 establishes prevalence and risk factors, C106 shows protective effects in mice with multiple citations, and C107 acknowledges contradictory findings (Ghabdian et al., 2022). The claims appropriately acknowledge complexity and conflicting results.

results.result: Epidemiological data suggests inverse correlation between helminth infections and asthma/allergy, but species-specific effects exist (A. lumbricoides increases risk). Clinical trials showed safety but minimal clinical benefit, possibly because helminths prevent rather than treat allergy.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C111 present a nuanced view of helminth-allergy relationships with appropriate citations. C108 establishes the general inverse correlation, C109 notes species-specific exceptions, C110 reports clinical trial results, and C111 offers a reasonable speculation (appropriately marked) about prevention vs. treatment. The claims acknowledge complexity and limitations.

results.result: An inverse relationship exists between helminth infection and insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, with chronic infection proposed to benefit host metabolism in adipose tissue, intestines, and liver.
results.evaluation: Claim C112 is supported by citations (van der Zande et al., 2019; Wiria et al., 2014) and extends the helminth-inflammatory disease relationship to metabolic disorders. The claim appropriately notes this is a proposed mechanism rather than definitively established causation.

results.result: Successful helminth therapy requires precise patient selection and helminth species matching. Identifying and characterizing helminth molecules and their target pathways offers opportunities for developing nature-inspired therapeutics, including synthetic exosome-based miRNA delivery systems.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C115 present forward-looking conclusions with appropriate citations. C113 and C114 make reasonable inferences about therapeutic requirements and opportunities (appropriately marked), while C115 proposes synthetic exosome approaches (appropriately marked as speculation). The claims are well-supported by the preceding evidence and provide a roadmap for future research.
